page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m2.xlarge is a compute-oriented virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance allocates 4 virtual CPUs across 2 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled on a KVM hypervisor. System memory totals 8.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB RAM per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators, necessitating remote block storage attachments for persistent file systems. Baseline network connectivity provides up to 2 Gbps of throughput, with no complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Standardized benchmarks place this instance within lower performance brackets. The Intel Xeon 8163 architecture delivers a Geekbench single-core score of 948.0 and a multi-core score of 2039.0, reflecting bottom-quartile throughput. PassMark testing reports a CPU score of 3615.54 and a memory score of 1219.93, with large-block memory read bandwidth registering at 19.91 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 18.49 GB/sec. Application tests show 3.03 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.54 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. For small 135M parameter language models, prompt processing reaches 235.39 tokens per second and text generation yields 57.14 tokens per second.

Given the legacy CPU generation and modest memory density, this instance functions as a low-overhead entry option for workloads requiring dedicated vCPUs with a minimal RAM footprint. The absence of local NVMe storage and basic 2 Gbps networking bound its data transfer capability. It is suited for basic compute jobs, lightweight container hosting, development or staging environments, background task queues, and low-traffic web services that do not demand extensive memory capacity or modern vector instruction extensions.
